pairs.why: B has printed number and operator keys, a wide display and a solar strip like the real calculator, while A's keys are blank and read like a generic toy.
B is a chunky close-up of the pier with smooth posts, coiled rope and a lifebuoy, like the real card, while A is a small distant pier over heavily textured water.
A's softer, semi-matte purple-navy shading matches the real cards' finish, while B's black hat is glossier and reads more like a statue.
B has the warm, lively, inviting look of the real building cards (lit door, steps, rounded shapes), while A is a cold grey scene with grainy crater texture.
A keeps the smooth, clean blue plastic of the real bottle, while B adds water-droplet surface detail that the real card doesn't have.
A's simple setting and smoother rounded spiral tiers are closer to the real topiary, while B adds a crowded set of props and busier leaf texture.
A's closed beak and calmer, rounded toy build are slightly closer to the real spring duck than B's open-mouthed cartoon face.
A's chunkier table with bigger board squares is slightly closer to the real chess table's bold proportions than B's finer, busier grid.
